name: Aaron and Miriam
charge: Speaking against Moses; challenging his authority
summary: Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses, using his marriage as a pretext to ask whether the Lord had not also spoken through them. God summoned all three and answered plainly.
offense: The occasion is named and it was a pretext: Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married (Numbers 12:1). That is Zipporah, the daughter of the priest of Midian, whom he had married in the forty years outside Egypt and whom the Lord had allowed him; they had said nothing about her when he was bringing them out of Egypt, nor when he set Aaron over the men and Miriam over the women. What they actually said is the charge: hath the Lord indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us? And the Lord heard it (Numbers 12:2). It was a claim of equality with the man God had set over them, and Miriam is named first because she led it. The record answers it before the Lord does, with the one line Moses did not write about himself: now the man Moses was very meek, above all the men which were upon the face of the earth (Numbers 12:3).

entries.commentary: Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married. This is still Zipporah, the daughter of the priest of Midian, whom Moses married in the forty years he dwelt outside Egypt, and whom the Lord allowed him to marry; a place being called Midian and the woman called an Ethiopian is no contradiction. They did not speak against Moses when he was saving them out of Egypt, nor when he set Aaron over the men and Miriam over the women; the murmuring came from somewhere else and they took hold of it. They said, Hath the LORD indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us? And the LORD heard it.

The man Moses was very meek, above all the men which were upon the face of the earth. The Lord suddenly called Moses, Aaron, and Miriam to the tabernacle, came down in the pillar of the cloud, and called Aaron and Miriam forth. He declared the difference: to a prophet He makes Himself known in a vision and speaks in a dream, but with His servant Moses, faithful in all His house, He speaks mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches. Wherefore then were ye not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?

The anger of the Lord was kindled, and the cloud departed from off the tabernacle, and Miriam became leprous, white as snow. Aaron pleaded, Lay not the sin upon us; and Moses cried unto the Lord, Heal her now, O God, I beseech thee. The Lord answered that if her father had but spit in her face, she should be ashamed seven days; so she was shut out from the camp seven days, and the people journeyed not till Miriam was brought in again. The spit is correction, a father putting his child in her place; had she been raised to respect the men of the Lord, this would not have befallen her. This is a charge to raise children in the fear of the Lord and to teach them to respect the elders and the men of the Lord. Parents who let their children speak evil to the men of the Lord provoke them to wrath and bring judgment on the household.

When a man hath taken a wife and she find no favour in his eyes because he hath found some uncleanness in her, then let him write her a bill of divorcement, give it in her hand, and send her out of his house. Christ magnified this law: when the Pharisees asked why Moses then commanded to give a writing of divorcement, he said, Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives, but from the beginning it was not so. Whosoever shall put away his wife, except it be for fornication, and shall marry another, committeth adultery; and whoso marrieth her which is put away doth commit adultery.

If the latter husband hate her and write her a bill of divorcement, or if the latter husband die, her former husband which sent her away may not take her again to be his wife after that she is defiled, for that is abomination before the Lord. The question is whether a woman who leaves her husband and becomes another man's wife can be joined to the first again; the prophet asks the same thing: shall he return unto her again? shall not that land be greatly polluted?

When a man hath taken a new wife, he shall not go out to war, neither shall he be charged with any business; he shall be free at home one year and shall cheer up his wife which he hath taken. Make it plain: the first year, stay at home and make a baby. Husband and wife render due benevolence to one another; benevolence means good, it is a good thing. The war laws give the same understanding: the man that had betrothed a wife and not taken her was sent back to his house, lest he die in the battle and another man take her, for the Lord is the one that goeth with the host to fight against the enemies.

No man shall take the nether or the upper millstone to pledge, for he taketh a man's life to pledge. The millstone is a tool for grinding meal: the manna was gathered and ground in mills or beaten in a mortar and baked into cakes. Taking a man's tool takes away his living, like somebody stealing your tools so you cannot make a living. It is better that they steal your money, because with your tools you can go back and make more money.

Remember what the Lord thy God did unto Miriam by the way, after that ye were come forth out of Egypt: Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married, and Miriam was not supposed to be speaking against Moses. The anger of the Lord was kindled against them, the cloud departed from off the tabernacle, and behold, Miriam became leprous, white as snow. The Lord said, if her father had but spit in her face, should she not be ashamed seven days? Had her father chastised her and rebuked her sharply, she would not have had that tongue. That is for a lot of our sisters today who do not have that understanding.

When thou dost lend thy brother any thing, thou shalt not go into his house to fetch his pledge; stand abroad, and let the man bring the pledge out unto thee. If the man be poor, thou shalt not sleep with his pledge; deliver him the pledge again when the sun goeth down, that he may sleep in his own raiment and bless thee, and it shall be righteousness unto thee before the Lord thy God. The law was already given: if thou at all take thy neighbour's raiment to pledge, deliver it by that the sun goeth down, for that is his covering only, and when he crieth unto the Most High, he will hear, for he is gracious. The history shows how wicked we were to each other: Israel laid themselves down upon clothes laid to pledge by every altar, stacking up people's raiment like pallets and drinking the wine of the condemned in the house of their god, instead of returning the pledge before the sun went down as righteousness. That is why the Lord was judging us.

The fathers shall not be put to death for the children, neither shall the children be put to death for the fathers: every man shall be put to death for his own sin. The example: as soon as the kingdom was confirmed in Amaziah's hand, he slew his servants which had slain the king his father, but the children of the murderers he slew not, according unto that which is written in the book of the law of Moses. The soul that sinneth, it shall die: the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father, neither shall the father bear the iniquity of the son.

verses.text: And Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married: for he had married an Ethiopian woman.
And they said, Hath the Lord indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us? And the Lord heard it.
And he said, Hear now my words: If there be a prophet among you, I the Lord will make myself known unto him in a vision, and will speak unto him in a dream.
My servant Moses is not so, who is faithful in all mine house.
With him will I speak mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches; and the similitude of the Lord shall he behold: wherefore then were ye not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?
And the anger of the Lord was kindled against them; and he departed.
And the cloud departed from off the tabernacle; and, behold, Miriam became leprous, white as snow: and Aaron looked upon Miriam, and, behold, she was leprous.
And Moses cried unto the Lord, saying, Heal her now, O God, I beseech thee.
And the Lord said unto Moses, If her father had but spit in her face, should she not be ashamed seven days? let her be shut out from the camp seven days, and after that let her be received in again.
And Miriam was shut out from the camp seven days: and the people journeyed not till Miriam was brought in again.
Remember what the Lord thy God did unto Miriam by the way, after that ye were come forth out of Egypt.
